## Call

One phone call — connected or not.

### An attempt is a record

The most common modelling mistake here is writing a row **only when someone picks up**. Then *"we have called Dana four times and never reached her"* is unanswerable, and the next person calls a fifth time without knowing.

So `outcome` has six values and only one of them is `connected`:

```
connected · no-answer · voicemail · busy · wrong-number · failed
```

Everything downstream — follow-up rules, unreachable flags, call counts — reads the outcome rather than assuming a row means a conversation.

### Duration only means something when connected

`durationSeconds` on a `no-answer` is **ring time**: a different quantity wearing the same name.

`effectiveDuration` returns undefined unless the call connected, so an average-call-length figure cannot silently average in fifteen seconds of ringing. `durationLabel` follows it — a `2:14` next to a call nobody answered reads as a conversation that did not happen.

### `phoneNumber` is stored as dialled, not as displayed

E.164, from `NormalizePhoneCommand`. A call record whose number was stored as a human typed it cannot be matched against the contact it belongs to later — which is how one person's call history ends up split across three spellings of the same number.

### Notes are markdown, and separate from the outcome

The outcome is machine-readable; the note is what the human wants to say. Encoding *"left message about the invoice"* into an enum value loses it; putting the outcome only in prose makes it unqueryable. Both, separately.

### `regarding` is a link

So the call follows a rename, and opening it lands on the real record rather than a stale title.

### Presentation

The embedded row shows the duration where a connected call has one, and **the outcome where it does not** — the slot means *"what came of this"*, not *"how long"*. `wrong-number` and `failed` take the destructive hue; the rest stay muted, because a no-answer is ordinary.

### Non-goals

Does not dial. Does not record audio — `recordingUrl` is deliberately absent until there is a retention policy to attach to it. Not a meeting: a call has one channel and no agenda.
